4	  Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given
5	  the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole
6	  pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence
7	  conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions,
8	  bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the
9	  Program-Buffer CSR sweep, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill
10	  whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport /
11	  transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value
12	  table, which mode a CSR is supported in, csr_sweep cmderr faults, or
13	  --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say
14	  "bring-up" explicitly.
15	---
16	
17	# CSR transport bring-up for a new Andes core
18	
19	Inputs you need from the user (ask if missing):
20	- The AndeStar V5 SPA PDF for the core family (the repo carries
21	  `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf` for the current cores).
22	- The engine name (e.g. `ax45mpv_premium`) and a built vsim checkout
23	  (`VSIM_BIN_DIR` in `config.env` points at its `build/`).
24	- Optionally the matching QEMU `-cpu` name for the oracle leg.
25	
26	The goal: every CSR the core implements and the ROI can touch is restored at
27	resume, re-read at drain, and `--verify`-compared -- and every CSR the core
28	does NOT implement is gated off, because the batched Program-Buffer sweep
29	faults (cmderr=3) on a single over-claimed CSR.
30	
31	Work in this order. Each phase has a reference file with the details --
32	read it when you reach the phase, not before.
33	
34	## Phase 0: establish ground truth
35	
36	The engine's compiled-in config is the ONLY truth about what it implements.
37	Read `$VSIM_BIN_DIR/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc` (the BUILD directory copy --
38	the `external/` source tree can differ from what was actually built) and
39	`sim_<engine> --describe`. Do not trust QEMU: its gdbstub exposes CSRs the
40	vsim RTL does not implement (QEMU models a fuller core), and restoring or
41	sweeping one of those stalls or faults the Debug Module.
42	
43	## Phase 1: mine the spec
44	
45	Run `scripts/extract_csr_inventory.py <spec.pdf>` to refresh
46	`tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv` (needs PyMuPDF; use a venv). Then pull,
47	for each CSR the core claims: the IM Requirement (existence condition), the
48	Access Mode, and the reset value. The SPA has a fixed per-CSR layout and a
49	consolidated existence table (Table 13) -- see
50	`references/spec-mining.md` for the exact headers and extraction recipes.
51	
52	## Phase 2: classify dispositions
53	
54	Run `scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv` and
55	the guard `tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py`. The guard enforces
56	inventory == matrix == ABI (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`), so a CSR added to
57	the wire format without a disposition (or vice versa) fails loudly. New
58	transported CSRs are one X-macro line in `state_abi.h`
59	(`HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST` / `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST`); every consumer
60	(plugin drain, restore, drain re-read, verify) iterates the same list.
61	
62	## Phase 3: bind capability gates
63	
64	For each transported CSR, map its IM Requirement to a gate in the vsim
65	repo's `src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp` (address -> gate) and bind the gate to a
66	`_NDS_*` config macro in `andes_caps_config.hpp` (absent macro reads as
67	"off" -- never a compile error). The gate must encode the SPEC's existence
68	condition, not a plausibly-related feature; two real bugs came from getting
69	this wrong. Follow TDD: model the new engine's config shape as a caps
70	helper in `tests/hybrid/andes_caps.test.cpp` and write the failing
71	expectation first. Read `references/caps-gating.md` -- it carries the
72	hard-won rules and the write-prerequisite (setup ordering) requirements.
73	
74	## Phase 4: reset values and verify exclusions
75	
76	Two reset-value sources exist and they legitimately differ:
77	- The SPA reset table (documentation; many fields are IM = implementation
78	  determined or DC = don't care).
79	- The EMPIRICAL baseline the simulator drains from the freshly reset hart
80	  (cached per engine build + ELF). The liveness gate compares against this
81	  one -- it is self-truthing, so spec IM/DC values need no manual table.
82	
83	Where QEMU's reset differs from the engine's reset for a CSR the program
84	never writes (e.g. `msp_bound`, `milmb` enable bit), a strict compare
85	false-positives: add it to `andes_verify_excluded` in
86	`driver/state_diff.cpp` with a comment naming the divergence. Do NOT
87	exclude a CSR to hide a transport bug -- exclusion is only for
88	engine-implementation artifacts.
89	
90	## Phase 5: validate (the ladder)
91	
92	Run bottom-up; each rung catches what the one below cannot. The key
93	insight: the tolerant abstract path MASKS capability bugs (a faulting read
94	mirrors as zero, QEMU drains zero too, --verify falsely matches), so only
95	the batched CSR sweep truly validates the caps table -- it faults on an
96	over-claim and bisects to NAME the offending CSR. A cold-cache hybrid run
97	exercises it via the baseline capture. Full commands, expected outputs, and
98	failure playbook: `references/validation.md`.
99	
100	## Phase 6: commit and document
101	
102	TDD and Tidy First apply: caps fixes, sweep/transport changes, and docs are
103	separate commits, each on a green suite. Update the vsim `ROADMAP.md`
104	known-limits and `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` (section 4.4 documents what --verify
105	compares). Update `tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv` through the classifier,
106	never by hand -- the guard checks policy == matrix.

name: csr-transport-bringup
description: >
  Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given
  the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole
  pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence
  conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions,
  bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the
  Program-Buffer CSR sweep, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill
  whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport /
  transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value
  table, which mode a CSR is supported in, csr_sweep cmderr faults, or
  --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say
  "bring-up" explicitly.
---

# CSR transport bring-up for a new Andes core

Inputs you need from the user (ask if missing):
- The AndeStar V5 SPA PDF for the core family (the repo carries
  `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf` for the current cores).
- The engine name (e.g. `ax45mpv_premium`) and a built vsim checkout
  (`VSIM_BIN_DIR` in `config.env` points at its `build/`).
- Optionally the matching QEMU `-cpu` name for the oracle leg.

The goal: every CSR the core implements and the ROI can touch is restored at
resume, re-read at drain, and `--verify`-compared -- and every CSR the core
does NOT implement is gated off, because the batched Program-Buffer sweep
faults (cmderr=3) on a single over-claimed CSR.

Work in this order. Each phase has a reference file with the details --
read it when you reach the phase, not before.

## Phase 0: establish ground truth

The engine's compiled-in config is the ONLY truth about what it implements.
Read `$VSIM_BIN_DIR/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc` (the BUILD directory copy --
the `external/` source tree can differ from what was actually built) and
`sim_<engine> --describe`. Do not trust QEMU: its gdbstub exposes CSRs the
vsim RTL does not implement (QEMU models a fuller core), and restoring or
sweeping one of those stalls or faults the Debug Module.

## Phase 1: mine the spec

Run `scripts/extract_csr_inventory.py <spec.pdf>` to refresh
`tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv` (needs PyMuPDF; use a venv). Then pull,
for each CSR the core claims: the IM Requirement (existence condition), the
Access Mode, and the reset value. The SPA has a fixed per-CSR layout and a
consolidated existence table (Table 13) -- see
`references/spec-mining.md` for the exact headers and extraction recipes.

## Phase 2: classify dispositions

Run `scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv` and
the guard `tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py`. The guard enforces
inventory == matrix == ABI (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`), so a CSR added to
the wire format without a disposition (or vice versa) fails loudly. New
transported CSRs are one X-macro line in `state_abi.h`
(`HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST` / `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST`); every consumer
(plugin drain, restore, drain re-read, verify) iterates the same list.

## Phase 3: bind capability gates

For each transported CSR, map its IM Requirement to a gate in the vsim
repo's `src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp` (address -> gate) and bind the gate to a
`_NDS_*` config macro in `andes_caps_config.hpp` (absent macro reads as
"off" -- never a compile error). The gate must encode the SPEC's existence
condition, not a plausibly-related feature; two real bugs came from getting
this wrong. Follow TDD: model the new engine's config shape as a caps
helper in `tests/hybrid/andes_caps.test.cpp` and write the failing
expectation first. Read `references/caps-gating.md` -- it carries the
hard-won rules and the write-prerequisite (setup ordering) requirements.

## Phase 4: reset values and verify exclusions

Two reset-value sources exist and they legitimately differ:
- The SPA reset table (documentation; many fields are IM = implementation
  determined or DC = don't care).
- The EMPIRICAL baseline the simulator drains from the freshly reset hart
  (cached per engine build + ELF). The liveness gate compares against this
  one -- it is self-truthing, so spec IM/DC values need no manual table.

Where QEMU's reset differs from the engine's reset for a CSR the program
never writes (e.g. `msp_bound`, `milmb` enable bit), a strict compare
false-positives: add it to `andes_verify_excluded` in
`driver/state_diff.cpp` with a comment naming the divergence. Do NOT
exclude a CSR to hide a transport bug -- exclusion is only for
engine-implementation artifacts.

## Phase 5: validate (the ladder)

Run bottom-up; each rung catches what the one below cannot. The key
insight: the tolerant abstract path MASKS capability bugs (a faulting read
mirrors as zero, QEMU drains zero too, --verify falsely matches), so only
the batched CSR sweep truly validates the caps table -- it faults on an
over-claim and bisects to NAME the offending CSR. A cold-cache hybrid run
exercises it via the baseline capture. Full commands, expected outputs, and
failure playbook: `references/validation.md`.

## Phase 6: commit and document

TDD and Tidy First apply: caps fixes, sweep/transport changes, and docs are
separate commits, each on a green suite. Update the vsim `ROADMAP.md`
known-limits and `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` (section 4.4 documents what --verify
compares). Update `tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv` through the classifier,
never by hand -- the guard checks policy == matrix.

1	# Mining the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF
2	
3	## Extract text once, grep many times
4	
5	```sh
6	python -m venv /tmp/pdfvenv && /tmp/pdfvenv/bin/pip -q install pymupdf
7	/tmp/pdfvenv/bin/python - <<'EOF'
8	import fitz, sys
9	doc = fitz.open("AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf")
10	with open("/tmp/spa.txt", "w") as f:
11	    for i, page in enumerate(doc, 1):
12	        f.write(f"===PAGE {i}===\n" + page.get_text())
13	EOF
14	```
15	
16	The repo already automates the inventory step:
17	`scripts/extract_csr_inventory.py <spec.pdf> [out.csv]` writes
18	`tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv` (addr, privilege, name, mode, section).
19	Run it when the spec revision changes; the committed CSV is the checked-in
20	truth the coverage guard reads.
21	
22	## Per-CSR section layout (chapters 8-10)
23	
24	Every CSR gets a section with fixed headers -- grep for the mnemonic, then
25	read the block:
26	
27	```
28	8.3.8
29	User Scratch Register
30	Mnemonic Name: uscratch
31	IM Requirement: misa[13]==1 (N extension)     <- existence condition
32	Access Mode: User                              <- privilege mode
33	CSR Address: 0x040 (standard read/write)
34	XLEN: 64 and 32
35	<bit-field diagram: per-field name, type (RW/RO/W1C/...), reset value>
36	```
37	
38	- `IM Requirement:` is THE existence condition. This is what the caps gate
39	  must encode (Phase 3). "Always" means gate ALWAYS.
40	- `Access Mode:` gives the privilege mode the user asked about ("which mode
41	  supports this CSR"): Machine / Supervisor / User / Debug.
42	- Field types use the terminology page (chapter 9.1): IM = implementation
43	  determined, DC = reset value is don't care, RO/WO/RW/W1C/WS/RAZWI.
44	  IM and DC reset values CANNOT be tabled from the spec -- that is exactly
45	  why the empirical reset baseline (Phase 4) is the source the liveness
46	  gate uses.
47	
48	## Table 13: the consolidated existence table
49	
50	"Table 13: Existence configuration condition(s)" lists CSR groups against
51	their conditions in one place -- faster than walking every section, and the
52	authoritative cross-check when a per-section IM Requirement reads
53	ambiguously. Real rows:
54	
55	```
56	mcounterinten                 mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1
57	mcounterwen                   (mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1) & (misa[20]==1) // user
58	mcountermask_m
59	mcountermask_u
60	mcounterovf
61	mcountermask_s                (mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1) & (misa[18]==1) // supervisor
62	mcounteren                    misa[20]==1 // user mode
63	```
64	
65	Note the grouping: a condition line applies to the CSR names stacked above
66	it (PDF table extraction flattens the rows). `misa[20]` = U-mode present,
67	`misa[18]` = S-mode present. Cross-map to config.inc:
68	`NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 2` -> U-mode, `== 3` -> S-mode;
69	`mmsc_cfg.PMNDS` -> the Andes perf-monitor feature.
70	
71	## What "supported mode" means for transport
72	
73	The transport envelope is bare-metal, single-hart, trap-free ROI, M or M+U.
74	So:
75	- M-mode CSRs (`0x3xx`, `0x7xx`, `0xBxx` machine): transport candidates.

# Mining the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF

## Extract text once, grep many times

```sh
python -m venv /tmp/pdfvenv && /tmp/pdfvenv/bin/pip -q install pymupdf
/tmp/pdfvenv/bin/python - <<'EOF'
import fitz, sys
doc = fitz.open("AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf")
with open("/tmp/spa.txt", "w") as f:
    for i, page in enumerate(doc, 1):
        f.write(f"===PAGE {i}===\n" + page.get_text())
EOF
```

The repo already automates the inventory step:
`scripts/extract_csr_inventory.py <spec.pdf> [out.csv]` writes
`tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv` (addr, privilege, name, mode, section).
Run it when the spec revision changes; the committed CSV is the checked-in
truth the coverage guard reads.

## Per-CSR section layout (chapters 8-10)

Every CSR gets a section with fixed headers -- grep for the mnemonic, then
read the block:

```
8.3.8
User Scratch Register
Mnemonic Name: uscratch
IM Requirement: misa[13]==1 (N extension)     <- existence condition
Access Mode: User                              <- privilege mode
CSR Address: 0x040 (standard read/write)
XLEN: 64 and 32
<bit-field diagram: per-field name, type (RW/RO/W1C/...), reset value>
```

- `IM Requirement:` is THE existence condition. This is what the caps gate
  must encode (Phase 3). "Always" means gate ALWAYS.
- `Access Mode:` gives the privilege mode the user asked about ("which mode
  supports this CSR"): Machine / Supervisor / User / Debug.
- Field types use the terminology page (chapter 9.1): IM = implementation
  determined, DC = reset value is don't care, RO/WO/RW/W1C/WS/RAZWI.
  IM and DC reset values CANNOT be tabled from the spec -- that is exactly
  why the empirical reset baseline (Phase 4) is the source the liveness
  gate uses.

## Table 13: the consolidated existence table

"Table 13: Existence configuration condition(s)" lists CSR groups against
their conditions in one place -- faster than walking every section, and the
authoritative cross-check when a per-section IM Requirement reads
ambiguously. Real rows:

```
mcounterinten                 mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1
mcounterwen                   (mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1) & (misa[20]==1) // user
mcountermask_m
mcountermask_u
mcounterovf
mcountermask_s                (mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1) & (misa[18]==1) // supervisor
mcounteren                    misa[20]==1 // user mode
```

Note the grouping: a condition line applies to the CSR names stacked above
it (PDF table extraction flattens the rows). `misa[20]` = U-mode present,
`misa[18]` = S-mode present. Cross-map to config.inc:
`NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 2` -> U-mode, `== 3` -> S-mode;
`mmsc_cfg.PMNDS` -> the Andes perf-monitor feature.

## What "supported mode" means for transport

The transport envelope is bare-metal, single-hart, trap-free ROI, M or M+U.
So:
- M-mode CSRs (`0x3xx`, `0x7xx`, `0xBxx` machine): transport candidates.
- U-mode CSRs (`0x0xx`, `0x8xx`): transported only for the M+U envelope
  (disposition NEW_UDELTA) and gated on the UMODE gate.
- S-mode / Hypervisor / Debug-mode CSRs: excluded (EXCL_MODE / EXCL_DEBUG)
  until the S/U-envelope work needs them.
See `scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py`'s docstring for the full
disposition legend.

deliberate decision: ALWAYS only for base machine CSRs every Andes core
has (mxstatus, mclk_ctl, mdcause).

## The rules (each one paid for by a real bug)

1. **Gate on the spec's existence condition, exactly.** Not on a feature
   that usually comes along with it. `mcountermask_m` (0x7D1) exists when
   `(mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1) & (misa[20]==1)` -- it was wrongly gated
   PERF_MONITOR (the PMNDS half only); on the M-only premium

   feature and a privilege level, the privilege gate is the binding one for
   current engines -- match how the twins are gated (0x7D3/0x7CE were

2. **A standard-extension CSR is not implied by its Andes-classic
   sibling.** `jvt` (0x017) is Zcmt's table-jump base; classic Andes
   CoDense is `exec.it` + `uitb` (0x800). Gating jvt on CODENSE faulted the
   sweep on every CoDense core. When no config.inc knob exists for an
   extension, add the gate anyway bound to the macro it WOULD be
   (`_NDS_ZCMT_SUPPORT_INT`): absent reads as off today, and a future
   config turns it on without a code change.

3. **The tolerant abstract path masks over-claims -- do not trust a passing
   --verify as caps validation.** `read_register_64` clears a faulting
   read and mirrors it as zero; QEMU drains zero for a CSR the program
   never wrote; `--verify` matches zero == zero. Both bugs above were
   "verified" for months. The batched PB `csr_sweep` is the real
   validator: one over-claimed CSR faults the whole batch, and the sweep
   bisects to name it:
   `csr_sweep: CSR 0x17 raised cmderr -- the caps map over-claims a CSR
   the hart does not implement (fix andes_caps)`.

4. **QEMU-exposes != vsim-implements.** QEMU's `-cpu andes-ax45mpv` models
   full M+S+U and its gdbstub advertises CSRs the M-only RTL lacks.
   Capability is decided from vsim's config.inc, never from what QEMU
   drains. (To dump what QEMU really exposes: RSP
   `qXfer:features:read:riscv-csr.xml`.)

1. RED: in `tests/hybrid/andes_caps.test.cpp`, model the engine's
   config.inc shape as a helper (see `premium()`) -- set exactly the gates
   its `_NDS_*` macros turn on. Assert the expected `supports_csr()`
   verdicts, including the one that currently fails. Run in the vsim build
   container; show the failure.

   `andes_caps_config.hpp` if the gate is new). Comment the spec condition.

mis-modeled, as premium's perf monitor once was), fix the helper to match
`config.inc` -- the helper IS the machine-checked record of the engine
shape.

## Write requirements: what must be true before a restore can SET a CSR

  architectural V-CSR restore runs after the data sweep.

  write-enable before the counters it enables. `msp_bound`/`msp_base`
  before `mhsp_ctl` (enabling stack-safe with stale bounds traps).

  pinned.

  WARL-illegal field faults the batch, and unlike the drain there is no
  idempotent retry story for partially-applied writes. Restores go through

1	# The validation ladder
2	
3	Run bottom-up. Each rung catches what the one below cannot. All vsim
4	builds/tests run inside the vsim repo's container (built by its
5	`build_vsim.sh`); the andesim side runs on the host with `config.env`
6	providing `QEMU_BIN_DIR`/`VSIM_BIN_DIR`.
7	
8	## 1. Unit suite (seconds)
9	
10	```sh
11	podman run --rm -v <vsim-checkout>:/work -w /work localhost/vsim-env:latest \
12	  bash -c 'cmake --build build -j && ctest --test-dir build -LE hybrid-e2e'
13	```
14	
15	Catches: gate-map regressions (andes_caps tests), sweep encoding, X-macro
16	drift (`test_state_abi` pins the wire format size/offsets -- it changes
17	whenever a CSR list grows).
18	
19	## 2. Coverage guard (seconds, andesim repo)
20	
21	```sh
22	bash tests/andes_csr/test_csr_coverage_complete.sh
23	```
24	
25	Catches: inventory/matrix/ABI drift -- a CSR in the wire format without a
26	disposition, a disposition for a CSR the ABI dropped, or a hand-edited
27	matrix that the classifier policy does not reproduce.
28	
29	## 3. Cold-cache hybrid run = the caps validator (a minute)
30	
31	```sh
32	rm -rf ~/.cache/andesim   # force a fresh reset-baseline capture
33	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:<engine> \
34	  --verify tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf
35	```
36	
37	The capture is a FULL drain of the freshly reset hart and its CSR block
38	rides the batched PB sweep over the COMPLETE caps-supported list -- so a
39	clean capture empirically proves every claimed CSR is csrr-able on this
40	RTL. One over-claim aborts the run with the bisected name:
41	
42	```
43	[critical] fatal exception: csr_sweep: CSR 0x17 raised cmderr -- the caps
44	map over-claims a CSR the hart does not implement (fix andes_caps)
45	```
46	
47	Fix the named CSR's gate (see caps-gating.md), rebuild, rerun; repeat
48	until the capture is clean. Expect the `--verify` field count to DROP by
49	one per de-claimed CSR (e.g. premium went 146 -> 144 when 0x7D1 and 0x017
50	left the set) -- a drop is correct, those fields were zero-vs-zero
51	false matches before.
52	
53	## 4. --verify field diffs
54	
55	`[state-diff] FAIL` lines name mismatching fields. Triage order:
56	- Field never restored/re-read? Missing from an X-macro consumer (should
57	  be impossible if the lists are used) or caps-gated off on one side.
58	- Value differs only at reset (program never writes it)? Check
59	  QEMU-vs-engine reset divergence -> `andes_verify_excluded` in
60	  `driver/state_diff.cpp`, WITH a comment naming the divergence
61	  (precedents: msp_bound/msp_base all-ones-vs-zero, milmb/mdlmb enable
62	  bit, mip timer bit). Exclusion is for engine artifacts only -- never to
63	  hide a transport bug.
64	- Hardware counters that tick during the ROI (mhpmcounter*) are
65	  transported but verify-excluded by design, like mcycle.
66	
67	## 5. Full e2e matrix (minutes)
68	
69	```sh
70	QEMU_BIN_DIR=... VSIM_BIN_DIR=... VSIM_QEMU=... VSIM_QEMU32=... \
71	VSIM_PLUGIN=<andesim>/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so \
72	JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh
73	```
74	
75	Env vars must be on the command line (they do not persist between shells;
76	`source setup.sh` piped into anything loses its exports). JOBS=8 caps the
77	Verilator process count on big machines. Expect all tests green across
78	marker + pc + neg; the S/U fixtures (rt_priv_*) run on the S/U-capable
79	engine and take ~80 s each.
80	
81	## Cost model (why the sweep matters)
82	
83	Every Debug-Module operation (abstract command or PB exec) costs ~200-900
84	SIMULATED cycles at ~10 kHz wall speed, so full-drain wall-clock is
85	dominated by DM op COUNT, not bytes:
86	- GPR/FPR: PB block sweeps, ~6 round-trips each instead of 31/32 ops.
87	- Andes+M-ext CSRs: batched csrr+sd sweep, 3 CSRs per PB exec (progbufsize
88	  8 -> (8-1)/2), values ride the shared scratch page.
89	- Minimal drain (no --verify) skips all of it: only mcycle/minstret.
90	- The liveness gate (reset baseline) elides restores whose drained value
91	  equals the engine's reset value; the baseline is captured once per
92	  (engine build, ELF) and cached under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim/`
93	  (`--no-reset-baseline` to disable; the cache key includes the sim
94	  binary's mtime+size, so rebuilds self-invalidate).
95	
96	## Sweep/lift invariants (when touching the transport itself)
97	
98	- The drain sweep runs only on FULL drains; the simulator lifts the swept
99	  scratch bytes (`read_csr_from_scratch`) under EXACTLY the same condition
100	  the drain used to choose sweep-vs-abstract (`csr_scratch_fits`, flags,
101	  and not-minimal) -- a lift without a sweep reads garbage; a sweep
102	  without a lift silently loses in-ROI CSR writes.
103	- Scratch page layout (top page of RAM): V data grows up from the base;
104	  GPR block at the top, FPR below it, CSR block below that. Every user is
105	  fits-gated on the live vlenb so a full V page falls back to abstract
106	  ops on both sides symmetrically.
107
